A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Turbo-DDCM with the same authors, central method and research objectives. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original compression-quality and runtime experiments, method ablations, priority-aware reconstructions and distortion-control evaluations, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains original compression experiments and adds baseline comparisons, runtime decomposition, memory measurements, noise analysis and a diffusion-step ablation.

M1.justification: V2 extends priority-aware weighting to DDCM and DiffC, demonstrated in Figure S9, and reports an adaptation to optimal-transport flow-model parameterizations in Appendix A.1. The central Turbo-DDCM objective, atom-selection rule, noise normalization, bitstream scheme and distortion-control procedure remain intact.

E1.justification: Both versions use Kodak24, DIV2K and CLIC2020 for ordinary, priority-aware or distortion-controlled image compression. V1 already compresses CLIC2020 at multiple bitrates in Appendix G; v2's additional benchmark comparisons do not establish a new dataset or task. The resolution revisions concern evaluation settings.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated HiFiC, DiffEIC and StableCodec baselines to the existing non-zero-shot comparisons in Figure 4 and Tables 3–4. Figure S9 also adds priority-aware DDCM and DiffC variants to the regional-reconstruction comparison. This substantially expands the comparison set; IPIC is only discussed as related work.

E3.justification: The standard configuration changes from T=20 and M=5–700 to T=30 and M=45–300. Appendix A replaces the N=0–5 DDIM-step thresholds with a logarithmic-bin rule permitting N up to T−2. The principal DIV2K comparison changes from 768-pixel crops with SD 2.1 to 512-pixel crops with SD 2.1 Base. V2 also adds BD-PSNR and separate encoding/decoding timings, and changes the distortion-control target range from 19–24 to 21–25 dB.

E4.justification: V2 adds a T=20/30/40 quality-versus-runtime ablation, injected-noise covariance analysis, GPU-memory analysis, separate encoder/decoder profiling and priority-aware cross-method case studies. These address substantial additional questions about configuration choice, computational practicality and generality. Existing orthogonality, bitstream and distortion-control analyses are retained with revised results.

E5.justification: Appendix C.4 newly estimates the injected-noise covariance matrix, displayed in Figure S12. Otherwise uncertainty reporting remains stable: Appendix G retains 90% prediction intervals and mean-plus-standard-deviation displays. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or adds significance testing.

E6.justification: Figure 4 reports revised curves under changed configurations, including closer high-bitrate performance to DiffC. The headline runtime changes from 1.5 to 1.8 seconds, and the reported high-bitrate speedup over DDCM changes from over 40× to over 34×. New results include BD-PSNR matrices, CLIC2020 comparisons and approximately 3.05 GB peak memory. Existing labels also change, such as PerCo's building example from 0.002 to 0.031 BPP in v1 Figure S3 versus v2 Figure S2. Changed configurations prevent interpreting the revisions as controlled performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds a zero-mean derivation for the injected noise, absent from v1, and Appendix F explicitly formulates combination ranking and decoding. The existing thresholding derivation, complexity analysis and shared-objective mathematics remain. The new zero-mean argument does not justify moving codebook-dependent coefficients and normalization outside the expectation.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain fast zero-shot compression, efficient atom combination and encoding, and priority-aware and distortion-controlled variants. Quantified headline claims are moderated: round-trip time changes from 1.5 to 1.8 seconds, diffusion-step reduction from 95% to 92%, and speedup over the fastest prior method is described as nearly an order of magnitude.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies its quality comparison with an explicit StableCodec exception and identifies BPG, ILLM and StableCodec as faster alternatives. It adds interpretations concerning encoder/decoder contributions and approximately 20% memory overhead. The conclusion changes its better-quality competitor caveat from some zero-shot methods to some non-zero-shot methods; the latent encoder–decoder limitation remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds compression/decompression pseudocode, explicit codebook-seed construction, combination ranking/unranking details, scheduler selection, priority-aware configuration details and checkpoint identifiers for the new baselines. Appendix A.5 documents single-codebook residency and memory requirements. These substantially expand implementation guidance; the project-page link itself is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds focused references and discussion covering IPIC, flow matching, BD-PSNR and newly evaluated compression methods. It also acknowledges Su and Kasai's concurrent investigation of multiple selections from reproducible codebooks for inverse problems. The central positioning relative to DDCM and DiffC is retained.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing prose remain. V2 revises experimental discussion, adds targeted appendix subsections and a pseudocode appendix, corrects terminology and adds the conference-publication header. These are localized narrative and structural edits.

P2.justification: V2 adds seven numerical tables, algorithm displays and new timing, covariance, step-ablation and priority-aware figures. Figure 4 is substantially expanded, incorporating the earlier appendix DIV2K comparison alongside additional methods and runtime panels. Qualitative reconstructions are updated, and the orthogonality plot changes its horizontal axis from atom count to bitrate. Several other figures are retained through relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The broader baseline comparisons, separate encoding/decoding measurements, memory analysis and step-count ablation make the practical advantages and limitations more assessable. Expanded implementation documentation also improves transparency. However, new supporting material contains errors: Appendix C.4's zero-mean derivation unjustifiably extracts dependent quantities from expectations, and Appendix F's 0.01 BPP example conflicts with Equation 15, which gives approximately 0.108 BPP for the stated parameters. The stronger practical validation supports a limited net improvement, tempered by these mathematical and documentation weaknesses.
